name: Paycom Software, Inc.
moat_justification: ROIC proxy stayed 30.1–33.7% across FY2021–FY2023 and 30.5% in FY2025 (FY2024's 41.8% is flattered by the SBC-reversal credit) with gross margin stable at 82–85%, evidencing a real franchise built on payroll switching costs and a single-database architecture; capped at 6 because revenue growth decelerated to high single digits, its own Beti automation cannibalized a charged revenue line, and ADP/Paychex/Workday/Rippling press from both ends.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.4x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (6.7%) vs bull-case tier C (10.7%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: High-quality HCM franchise, moat 6/10, 30%+ ROIC — but at $253.00 it does not clear 15% on any scenario (weighted IRR 8.77%); it clears 15% only at or below the weighted IV@15% of $119.08.
moat_for: Payroll switching costs: mission-critical compliance/tax function, painful migration
Single-database architecture — one record per employee, no integration seams
ROIC proxy 30%+ for five straight years; gross margin ~83% stable
moat_against: Growth decelerated from ~30% to +7–8% guided; mid-market land-grab over
Beti automated away corrective-payroll charges — own product ate a revenue line
ADP/Paychex scale and compliance depth; Workday above, Rippling/Gusto below
Opaque per-module pricing and high setup fees — recurring buyer complaints
Founder concentration and US mid-market concentration
